FIRST DROPS: the first fat drops of rain darkening the stone one spot at a time, rings starting on the pool
RAIN THROUGH SUNLIGHT: a warm shower falling through bright sunlight, each drop catching gold as it passes the arch
EAVES BEGINNING TO DRIP: the rain easing now, the old eaves gathering the last of it into slow, heavy drops
SHOWER PASSING: the shower thinning to a silver haze, the wet stones beginning to shine in the returning light
STONE DARKENING: a gentle rain moving across the courtyard, darkening each pale stone in a slow, quiet tide
FLOCK LEAVING THE TOWER: a flock bursting from the tower top and scattering wide across the sky in small dark specks
BIRDS FROM THE WALL: small birds lifting off the old wall one after another, each one tilting up into the open air
STARLINGS RISING: a cloud of starlings lifting from the ivy and spreading softly across the pale evening sky
FLOCK TURNING: the flock wheeling together above the ruin, catching the light as they turn and vanish over the treeline
PETALS ON THE STAIR: blossom petals drifting down across the stair, settling into the cracks between the old stones
LEAVES TURNING DOWN: leaves turning slowly down through the still air, each one rocking gently before it comes to rest
SEEDS IN THE LIGHT: seeds floating bright where the afternoon sun reaches, rising and dipping on the faintest breath of air
PETAL ACROSS WATER: a single pale petal drifting out across the surface of the still pool, slow and silent
LOW SUN IN THE ARCH: the low sun just reaching the inside of the arch, laying a warm line of gold across the old stone floor
LAST LIGHT ON THE STONE: the last light touching the tallest standing stone, holding there a moment before it softly fades
SUN BEHIND THE RUIN: the sun slipping behind the ruin and edging every broken line in a fine, trembling gold
SUNLIGHT ON THE CAPITAL: late sun arriving at the carved capital, filling the worn detail with warm amber and soft shadow
RINGS ON THE POOL: rings spreading slowly across the still pool from a single drop, reaching the mossy edge and fading
THIN FALL GLITTERING: a thin fall of water picking up and glittering over the old stone lip in a bright, fine curtain
WAVE IN THE DOORWAY: a gentle wave washing through a sunken doorway, lifting the green weed and letting it settle again
MIST LIFTING: mist lifting off the valley below to show the old stone rising clear and pale into the morning air
MIST IN THE COURTYARD: a soft mist rolling gently through the courtyard, parting around the standing columns like slow water
MIST ON THE STEPS: a thin mist drifting across the lower steps, curling up around the carved base of the doorway
FIRST STARS: the first stars coming out one by one over the ruin, the sky deepening around them to a soft deep blue
FIREFLIES RISING: fireflies beginning to rise among the ferns at the base of the wall, drifting up into the warm still air
